# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tsamandouras_2024_brepocitinib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tsamandouras_2024_brepocitinib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-024-09901-2> (open access, PMC11136736)
* Supplement: Online Resource 1 of the article (NONMEM control stream `run6.mod`)

Tsamandouras et al. analysed the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) from
the phase 2a study of brepocitinib in plaque psoriasis (NCT02969018). The PASI
score divided by 72 was modelled with a zero-inflated beta distribution: a
point mass at PASI = 0 and a beta density on (0, 1) whose mean `mu` is the
model-predicted score. The expected score falls from an individual baseline
through an exponential placebo effect and a drug effect delivered through a
type I indirect-response latent variable `R(t)`, whose production the
individual average steady-state brepocitinib concentration `CAV` inhibits.

# Population

212 adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (PASI >= 12, PGA 3 or 4,
>= 10% body surface area involved) were randomized to eight arms: a 4-week
induction period with brepocitinib 30 or 60 mg once daily (QD) or placebo,
then an 8-week maintenance period with 10 or 30 mg QD, 100 mg once weekly (QW)
or placebo (Table 1 and Figure 1 of the paper). The participants were 69.8%
male and 89.2% White, with median age 48 years (18-75), median weight 91.6 kg
(45.1-204.3) and median baseline PASI 18.2 (12-54). Only PASI scores from weeks
0-12 were analysed, and no covariates were tested.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Tsamandouras_2024_brepocitinib")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table collects them, together with the equations.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `logitrbase` (BSL) | logit((18.00 - 12) / 60) | Table 2 BSL = 18.00; Eq. 14 with bounds 12 and 72 |
| `imax` | 1 (fixed) | Online Resource 1 `$THETA` '1 FIX ; IMAX' |
| `lic50` (IC50) | log(53.24) ng/mL | Table 2 |
| `lkout` (kout = kin) | log(0.067) 1/day | Table 2 and its footnote |
| `logitpmax` (Pmax) | logit(0.489) | Table 2; Online Resource 1 `LGPMAX` |
| `lkpbo` (kp) | log(0.047) 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lphi` (phi) | log(31.25) | Table 2 |
| `logite0_pasi0` (zeta1) | 2.228 | Table 2 |
| `e_mu_pasi0` (zeta2) | 62.67 | Table 2 |
| `etalogitrbase` | 1.655 | Table 2 'etaBSL omega2' |
| Average concentration `CAV = Dose / (CL/F * tau)` | -- | Eq. 1 |
| Transformed score `y = PASI / 72` | -- | Eq. 2 |
| Zero-inflated beta density | -- | Eq. 3-4 |
| Nemes approximation to the gamma function | -- | Eq. 5; Online Resource 1 `LGAMMAX1-3` |
| `alpha = mu * phi`, `beta = (1 - mu) * phi` | -- | Eq. 6-7 |
| `mu = (BSL - fp(t) - fd(t)) / 72` | -- | Eq. 9 |
| `fp(t) = BSL * Pmax * (1 - exp(-kp * t))` | -- | Eq. 10 |
| `fd(t) = BSL * (1 - Pmax) * (1 - R(t))` | -- | Eq. 11 |
| `dR/dt = kin * (1 - CAV / (IC50 + CAV)) - kout * R`, `R(0) = 1` | -- | Eq. 12 |
| `p0 = expit(zeta1 - zeta2 * mu)` | -- | Eq. 13 |
| Logit-normal IIV on the baseline, bounds 12 and 72 | -- | Eq. 14; Online Resource 1 `LGBASE` |

# Exposure input: CAV from the Hughes 2022 population PK model

The paper derives each participant's `CAV` from the empirical Bayes CL/F of the
brepocitinib population PK model of Hughes et al. (2022), shipped as
`modellib("Hughes_2022_brepocitinib")`: CL/F = 18.7 L/h at 70 kg, a fixed
weight exponent of 0.75 and 78% CV. Its clinical trial simulations sample CL/F
from that distribution after applying each simulated participant's weight. The
code below does the same, taking the typical value, exponent and variance from
the shipped PK model.

```{r pk-inputs}
pk <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Hughes_2022_brepocitinib"))
cl_typ <- exp(pk$theta[["lcl"]])
e_wt_cl <- pk$theta[["e_wt_cl"]]
omega_cl <- pk$omega["etalcl", "etalcl"]
c(cl_typ = cl_typ, e_wt_cl = e_wt_cl, omega_cl = omega_cl)

# Dose in mg, CL/F in L/h, tau in h; x 1000 gives ng/mL (Eq. 1).
cav_ngml <- function(dose_mg, cl_lh, tau_h) dose_mg * 1000 / (cl_lh * tau_h)
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper sampled weights with replacement from the study dataset, which is not
public. The cohort here draws log-normal weights around the reported median of
91.6 kg, truncated to the observed 45.1-204.3 kg range. All random numbers come
from base R after `set.seed()`, and the between-subject random effects are
passed to `rxSolve()` through `params`, so the cohort does not depend on the
rxode2 build or thread count. The same 200 participants are used in every arm,
which makes the arm comparisons paired.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20240302)
n_per_arm <- 200
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Tsamandouras_2024_brepocitinib"))

cohort <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n(), log(91.6), 0.22)), 45.1), 204.3),
    cl = cl_typ * (WT / 70)^e_wt_cl * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, sqrt(omega_cl))),
    etalogitrbase = rnorm(n(), 0, sqrt(mod$omega["etalogitrbase", "etalogitrbase"]))
  )
summary(cohort$WT)
```

The observation step draws the score from the zero-inflated beta distribution:
PASI = 0 with probability `p0_pasi`, otherwise `72 * Beta(alpha_pasi,
beta_pasi)`.

```{r helpers}
# Simulate one regimen in the cohort. `ind` and `maint` are the regimens of the
# induction (days 0-27) and maintenance (day 28 on) periods: dose in mg and
# dosing interval in h (24 for QD, 168 for QW); dose 0 is placebo.
sim_regimen <- function(label, ind, maint, times) {
  cav_ind <- cav_ngml(ind$dose, cohort$cl, ind$tau)
  cav_maint <- cav_ngml(maint$dose, cohort$cl, maint$tau)
  events <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = times) |>
    mutate(
      evid = 0L,
      amt = 0,
      # CAV is carried forward from each row, so the value on the day-28 row
      # is the maintenance exposure from day 28 onwards.
      CAV = ifelse(time < 28, cav_ind[id], cav_maint[id])
    )
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
    events = events,
    params = cohort[, c("id", "etalogitrbase")],
    covsInterpolation = "locf",
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  sim$regimen <- label
  sim$CAV <- events$CAV
  sim
}

draw_pasi <- function(sim) {
  zero <- runif(nrow(sim)) < sim$p0_pasi
  sim$pasi <- ifelse(zero, 0, 72 * rbeta(nrow(sim), sim$alpha_pasi, sim$beta_pasi))
  sim
}

responders <- function(sim) {
  base <- sim |>
    filter(time == 0) |>
    select(regimen, id, pasi_bl = pasi)
  sim |>
    inner_join(base, by = c("regimen", "id")) |>
    mutate(pct_imp = 100 * (1 - pasi / pasi_bl)) |>
    group_by(regimen, time) |>
    summarise(
      PASI50 = 100 * mean(pct_imp >= 50),
      PASI75 = 100 * mean(pct_imp >= 75),
      PASI90 = 100 * mean(pct_imp >= 90),
      PASI100 = 100 * mean(pct_imp >= 100),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

qd <- function(dose) list(dose = dose, tau = 24)
qw <- function(dose) list(dose = dose, tau = 168)
```

# Likelihood check

`ll(pasi)` encodes the zero-inflated beta log-likelihood exactly as the
paper's control stream does, including the Nemes approximation to the log
gamma function. Solving the model with a `DV` column and comparing against a
closed form computed in R from the same `mu`, `phi` and `p0` confirms the
encoding.

```{r ll-check}
nemes <- function(x) {
  x * (log(x) - 1) + 0.5 * (log(2 * 3.1415) - log(x)) +
    1.25 * x * log(1 + 1 / (15 * x^2))
}
ll_events <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = c(0, 14, 28, 56, 84, 84),
  evid = 0L,
  amt = 0,
  CAV = 54.5,
  DV = c(18, 12.3, 0, 4.2, 0.6, 0)
)
ll_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ll_events, returnType = "data.frame")
ll_ref <- with(ll_sim, ifelse(
  DV == 0,
  log(p0_pasi),
  nemes(phi) - nemes(alpha_pasi) - nemes(beta_pasi) +
    (alpha_pasi - 1) * log(DV / 72) + (beta_pasi - 1) * log(1 - DV / 72) +
    log(1 - p0_pasi)
))
ll_exact <- with(ll_sim, ifelse(
  DV == 0,
  log(p0_pasi),
  dbeta(DV / 72, alpha_pasi, beta_pasi, log = TRUE) + log(1 - p0_pasi)
))
ll_sim |>
  mutate(ll_closed_form = ll_ref, ll_exact_gamma = ll_exact) |>
  select(time, DV, mu_pasi, p0_pasi, ll_pasi, ll_closed_form, ll_exact_gamma) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5)

# The model's ll and the R closed form use the same inputs, so they must agree
# to floating-point precision.
stopifnot(max(abs(ll_sim$ll_pasi - ll_ref)) < 1e-8)
```

The last column replaces the Nemes approximation with the exact log gamma
function. The two agree closely while the beta shapes are above 1, and the
approximation drifts when a shape falls well below 1 (a predicted score of a
few tenths of a point); the parameter estimates were obtained with the
approximation, so the model keeps it.

# Clinical trial simulation: week-16 responder rates (Figure 5)

The paper simulated placebo and brepocitinib 5-60 mg QD for 16 weeks with 56
participants per arm and 2000 trials, assessing PASI at baseline and every 2
weeks. One trial of 200 participants per arm is simulated here for placebo,
10, 30 and 60 mg QD.

```{r fig5-sim}
times_16 <- seq(0, 112, by = 14)
flat_doses <- c(0, 10, 30, 60)
sim16 <- bind_rows(lapply(flat_doses, function(d) {
  lbl <- if (d == 0) "Placebo QD" else paste(d, "mg QD")
  sim_regimen(lbl, qd(d), qd(d), times_16)
})) |>
  draw_pasi()

resp16 <- responders(sim16) |>
  filter(time == 112)

cav_med <- sim16 |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(sim = median(CAV), .groups = "drop")
```

The median `CAV` matches the values in the bottom panels of Figure 5:

```{r fig5-cave}
cav_cmp <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("10 mg QD", "30 mg QD", "60 mg QD"),
  paper = c(18.1, 54.5, 108.6)
) |>
  inner_join(cav_med, by = "regimen") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - paper) / paper)
cav_cmp |>
  rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    "Paper median CAV (ng/mL)" = paper,
    "Simulated median CAV (ng/mL)" = sim,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# The median CAV is set by the typical CL/F at the 91.6 kg median weight; a
# wrong CL/F, weight exponent or unit conversion moves it by far more.
stopifnot(all(abs(cav_cmp$pct_diff) < 15))
```

The week-16 responder rates against the medians printed on Figure 5:

```{r fig5-table}
paper16 <- data.frame(
  regimen = rep(c("Placebo QD", "10 mg QD", "30 mg QD", "60 mg QD"), each = 3),
  metric = rep(c("PASI75", "PASI90", "PASI100"), 4),
  paper = c(
    12.5, 1.8, 0.0,
    35.7, 12.5, 5.4,
    62.5, 35.7, 21.4,
    78.6, 55.4, 35.7
  )
)
cmp16 <- resp16 |>
  pivot_longer(c(PASI75, PASI90, PASI100), names_to = "metric", values_to = "sim") |>
  inner_join(paper16, by = c("regimen", "metric")) |>
  mutate(diff = sim - paper) |>
  arrange(match(regimen, unique(paper16$regimen)), match(metric, c("PASI75", "PASI90", "PASI100")))
cmp16 |>
  select(regimen, metric, paper, sim, diff) |>
  rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    Metric = metric,
    "Paper, week 16 (%)" = paper,
    "Simulated, week 16 (%)" = sim,
    "Difference (percentage points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed IC50, kout, Pmax or zeta moves every arm by well over
  # this; one 200-subject trial has a binomial SE of about 3.5 points.
  abs(median(cmp16$diff)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(cmp16$diff), 0.9) < 10
)
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates the top panels of Figure 5 of Tsamandouras 2024 for placebo, 10, 30 and 60 mg QD: week-16 responder rates (points: this simulation; crosses: medians printed on the paper's figure)."}
cmp16 |>
  mutate(
    dose = c("Placebo QD" = 0, "10 mg QD" = 10, "30 mg QD" = 30, "60 mg QD" = 60)[regimen],
    metric = factor(metric, levels = c("PASI75", "PASI90", "PASI100"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(dose)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sim)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = sim)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = paper), shape = 4, size = 3, colour = "darkorange") +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg QD)", y = "Responders at week 16 (%)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Flat dosing versus induction and maintenance (Figure 6)

The paper compared 10, 30 and 60 mg QD for 16 weeks against 60 mg QD for 4
weeks followed by 10 or 30 mg QD for 12 weeks, and found that the
induction-maintenance regimens converge to the matching flat dose by week 16.

```{r fig6-sim}
sim_im <- bind_rows(
  sim_regimen("60 mg QD / 10 mg QD", qd(60), qd(10), times_16),
  sim_regimen("60 mg QD / 30 mg QD", qd(60), qd(30), times_16)
) |>
  draw_pasi()
sim6 <- bind_rows(filter(sim16, regimen != "Placebo QD"), sim_im)

pasi6 <- sim6 |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(median_pasi = median(pasi), .groups = "drop")
resp6 <- responders(sim6)
```

```{r fig6-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6 of Tsamandouras 2024: median PASI and PASI75/90/100 responder rates over 16 weeks for flat dosing and for 4 weeks of 60 mg QD induction followed by 10 or 30 mg QD."}
bind_rows(
  pasi6 |> transmute(regimen, time, panel = "Median PASI", value = median_pasi),
  resp6 |>
    pivot_longer(c(PASI75, PASI90, PASI100), names_to = "panel") |>
    select(regimen, time, panel, value)
) |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = c("Median PASI", "PASI75", "PASI90", "PASI100"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, value, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Week", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Because the cohorts are paired, the mean of the individual predicted scores
(before the zero-inflated beta draw) isolates the regimen effect. With kout = 0.067/day the latent variable re-equilibrates with
a half-life of about 10 days, so 12 weeks of maintenance erase the induction:

```{r fig6-typical}
typ <- sim6 |>
  filter(time == 112) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(mean_pasi_pred = mean(pasi_pred), .groups = "drop")
typ |>
  rename(Regimen = regimen, "Mean predicted PASI at week 16" = mean_pasi_pred) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

conv <- with(typ, c(
  ten = mean_pasi_pred[regimen == "60 mg QD / 10 mg QD"] / mean_pasi_pred[regimen == "10 mg QD"] - 1,
  thirty = mean_pasi_pred[regimen == "60 mg QD / 30 mg QD"] / mean_pasi_pred[regimen == "30 mg QD"] - 1
))
conv
# Same participants and parameters in both regimens, so the difference is the
# residual induction effect alone: exp(-0.067 * 84) is about 0.4%.
stopifnot(all(abs(conv) < 0.01))
```

# Study-design simulation (Figures 3 and 4)

The eight arms of the phase 2a study, with the induction regimen up to week 4
and the maintenance regimen from week 5 to week 12, simulated at the study's
assessment weeks (0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12).

```{r study-sim}
times_12 <- c(0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) * 7
arms <- list(
  list("Placebo QD", qd(0), qd(0)),
  list("30 mg QD / 10 mg QD", qd(30), qd(10)),
  list("30 mg QD / 100 mg QW", qd(30), qw(100)),
  list("30 mg QD", qd(30), qd(30)),
  list("60 mg QD / Placebo QD", qd(60), qd(0)),
  list("60 mg QD / 10 mg QD", qd(60), qd(10)),
  list("60 mg QD / 100 mg QW", qd(60), qw(100)),
  list("60 mg QD / 30 mg QD", qd(60), qd(30))
)
arm_levels <- vapply(arms, `[[`, character(1), 1)
sim12 <- bind_rows(lapply(arms, function(a) sim_regimen(a[[1]], a[[2]], a[[3]], times_12))) |>
  draw_pasi() |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = arm_levels))
```

The simulated baseline PASI agrees with the study's median of 18.2 and arm means
of 19.1-23.8 (Table 1):

```{r baseline-check}
bl <- sim12 |>
  filter(time == 0, regimen == "Placebo QD")
c(median = median(bl$pasi), mean = mean(bl$pasi))
stopifnot(abs(median(bl$pasi) - 18.2) / 18.2 < 0.1)
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates the simulated percentiles of Figure 3 of Tsamandouras 2024: median and 5th-95th percentiles of PASI by arm. The dashed line marks the end of the induction period."}
sim12 |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(pasi, 0.05),
    p50 = median(pasi),
    p95 = quantile(pasi, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "darkorange", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "darkorange3") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "PASI") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r responder-plot, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates the model predictions of Figure 4 of Tsamandouras 2024: PASI50/75/90/100 responder rates by arm over the 12-week treatment period."}
responders(sim12) |>
  pivot_longer(c(PASI50, PASI75, PASI90, PASI100), names_to = "metric") |>
  mutate(
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = arm_levels),
    metric = factor(metric, levels = c("PASI50", "PASI75", "PASI90", "PASI100"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, value, colour = metric)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Responders (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# NCA

The model has no drug concentrations: exposure enters as the per-period average
steady-state concentration `CAV`, so there is no concentration-time profile for
PKNCA. Validation is against the paper's simulated responder rates and median
`CAV` instead.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Exposure input.** `CAV` is a covariate in ng/mL, one value per treatment
  period, computed as Dose / (CL/F x tau) (Eq. 1). The model does not contain
  the brepocitinib PK model; use `modellib("Hughes_2022_brepocitinib")` to
  derive CL/F, as above. The simulations here use the weight-adjusted typical
  CL/F with its 78% CV and ignore the other Hughes 2022 covariates (Asian race,
  food, dose of 175 mg or more), as the paper's simulations did.
* **Weights.** The paper resampled weights from the study dataset, which is not
  available; a log-normal distribution with the reported median, truncated to
  the reported range, stands in for it.
* **Fixed-to-zero random effects.** The control stream carries etas on Imax,
  IC50, kout, Pmax and kp with variance fixed at 0; they are omitted, so the
  only random effect is on the baseline.
* **Imax.** Kept as `imax <- fixed(1)` because the control stream carries it as
  a fixed THETA; it does not change any prediction.
* **Likelihood.** `ll(pasi)` reads the observed score from `DV` on the 0-72
  scale and divides by 72, so the objective function equals the paper's -2LL.
  It uses the Nemes approximation to the log gamma function with the control
  stream's 3.1415 for pi; the constant cancels from the likelihood's dependence
  on the parameters. `rxSolve()` does not draw from this likelihood, so the
  vignette draws PASI from the zero-inflated beta distribution in R using the
  `p0_pasi`, `alpha_pasi` and `beta_pasi` outputs.
* **Time.** Time is in days from the first dose (kout and kp are per day). The
  PD switches from the induction to the maintenance exposure at day 28.
* **Placebo.** Placebo periods carry `CAV = 0`; the placebo effect acts in every
  arm.
* **Simulation size.** One trial of 200 participants per arm instead of 2000
  trials of 56, so the comparisons with Figure 5 carry binomial noise of a few
  percentage points.
